stem: A payments processor's backend team stores a database password that compliance requires to rotate automatically on a fixed schedule, with the rotation Lambda updating both the secret and the database together, without a maintenance window.

choices.text: Store the password as an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameter
Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured
Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager, but leave automatic rotation turned off and update it from the console when needed
Store the password as an AWS AppConfig configuration profile and deploy updates to it through AppConfig

rationale: AWS Secrets Manager is built to rotate a stored secret automatically on a schedule, using a rotation function that updates the secret and the backing database together, which is exactly the compliance requirement here. Parameter Store can hold the same value as a SecureString parameter, but it has no built-in scheduled rotation, so the password would still need a separate process to change. Storing the password in Secrets Manager but leaving rotation turned off drops the one requirement that matters most: nothing changes the password automatically, so it is no different from a value that never rotates. AWS AppConfig deploys configuration and feature-flag data to an application on a schedule the team controls; it has no credential-rotation capability and does not update a database's password as part of a deployment.
